title: Talks at a seminar
text: Six speakers, Ayesha, Bilal, Danish, Farah, Hamza and Imran, give one talk each at a seminar in Lahore, one after another, from first to sixth. Ayesha speaks before Bilal. Danish speaks immediately after Farah. Hamza speaks neither first nor last. Imran speaks before Farah.

stem: Which one of the following could be the order of speakers, from first to sixth?
options: Ayesha, Bilal, Farah, Danish, Hamza, Imran
Ayesha, Imran, Hamza, Farah, Danish, Bilal
Ayesha, Bilal, Danish, Hamza, Imran, Farah
Bilal, Ayesha, Hamza, Imran, Farah, Danish
explanation: Test each option against the rules. Ayesha, Imran, Hamza, Farah, Danish, Bilal satisfies every one. Each of the others breaks at least one rule: Bilal speaks before Ayesha; Danish does not follow Farah immediately; Farah speaks before Imran.

stem: Which one of the following cannot be true?
explanation: Imran must speak before Farah, so Farah cannot be first. The other three can happen: Ayesha, Imran, Hamza, Bilal, Farah, Danish has Danish sixth; Ayesha, Bilal, Hamza, Imran, Farah, Danish has Bilal second; Ayesha, Imran, Farah, Danish, Hamza, Bilal has Hamza fifth.

stem: If Hamza speaks second, which one of the following must be true?
explanation: Imran and Farah both speak before Danish, so at least two speakers precede him. With Hamza second, those two cannot be first and second together, so Danish is at least fourth and certainly after Hamza. The others fail in valid orders such as Ayesha, Hamza, Imran, Bilal, Farah, Danish, where Bilal comes after Imran and Farah is fifth, and Imran, Hamza, Ayesha, Bilal, Farah, Danish, where Ayesha is not first.

stem: If Bilal speaks before Imran, which one of the following must be true?
explanation: Ayesha, Bilal, Imran and Farah are now in a fixed order, and Danish follows Farah directly. Hamza cannot be first or last, so he goes into places two to four, never between Farah and Danish. Farah is therefore always fifth and Danish sixth. Hamza may be second, third or fourth, so the other options are not forced.

stem: If Farah speaks second, which one of the following could be true?
explanation: Farah second forces Imran first and Danish third. Ayesha, Hamza and Bilal then fill places four to six with Ayesha before Bilal and Hamza not last, so Hamza must be fourth or fifth. Hamza fourth works (Ayesha fifth, Bilal sixth). Bilal fifth would leave Hamza sixth, Ayesha third is taken by Danish, and Hamza sixth is not allowed.

title: Six chairs in a row
text: Six friends, Kiran, Nadia, Omar, Rabia, Saad and Tariq, sit in a row of six chairs numbered 1 to 6 from left to right at a cricket match in Karachi. Kiran and Nadia sit in neighbouring chairs. Omar sits somewhere to the left of Rabia. Saad does not sit at either end of the row. Tariq sits at one end of the row. Rabia and Saad do not sit in neighbouring chairs.

stem: Which one of the following could be the seating, from chair 1 to chair 6?
options: Kiran, Nadia, Omar, Saad, Tariq, Rabia
Kiran, Saad, Nadia, Omar, Rabia, Tariq
Tariq, Saad, Omar, Kiran, Nadia, Rabia
Kiran, Nadia, Omar, Rabia, Saad, Tariq
explanation: Test each option against the rules. Tariq, Saad, Omar, Kiran, Nadia, Rabia satisfies every one. Each of the others breaks at least one rule: Kiran and Nadia are not neighbours; Tariq sits in a middle chair; Rabia and Saad are neighbours.

stem: Which one of the following cannot be true?
explanation: Omar sits to the left of Rabia, so Omar cannot take chair 6, the last place on the right. Rabia in chair 2 (Omar, Rabia, Kiran, Nadia, Saad, Tariq), Kiran in chair 6 (Tariq, Saad, Omar, Rabia, Nadia, Kiran) and Saad in chair 5 (the same order as the first) all occur in valid seatings.

stem: If Tariq sits in chair 6, which one of the following must be true?
options: Saad does not sit in chair 4
explanation: With Tariq in chair 6, Saad must be in chair 2, 3 or 5. Suppose Saad is in chair 4: chairs 1, 2, 3 and 5 are left for Kiran, Nadia, Omar and Rabia. Kiran and Nadia must be neighbours, so they take 1 and 2 or 2 and 3. Rabia cannot be in chair 3 or 5 (next to Saad) and must be right of Omar, so Omar is 1 and Rabia 2, which leaves Kiran and Nadia in chairs 3 and 5, not neighbours. So Saad is never in chair 4. Each other option fails in a valid seating, for example Omar, Rabia, Kiran, Nadia, Saad, Tariq.

stem: If Kiran sits in chair 3, which one of the following could be true?
explanation: Kiran in chair 3 puts Nadia in chair 2 or 4. Nadia in chair 5 is impossible because it is not next to chair 3, Saad in chair 6 and Tariq in chair 4 break the rules about ends, while Rabia in chair 2 works in Omar, Rabia, Kiran, Nadia, Saad, Tariq.

stem: If Omar sits in chair 1, which one of the following must be true?
explanation: Tariq must sit at an end. With Omar in chair 1, that end is taken, so Tariq is in chair 6. The other options are possible but not forced: Omar, Rabia, Kiran, Nadia, Saad, Tariq has Saad in chair 5 and Rabia in chair 2; Omar, Saad, Kiran, Nadia, Rabia, Tariq has Rabia in chair 5; Omar, Rabia, Nadia, Kiran, Saad, Tariq has Nadia in chair 3.

title: Club sessions this week
text: A school in Multan holds six club sessions in one week, one on each day from Monday to Saturday. The sessions are Quiz, Debate, Art, Chess, Calligraphy and Drama. Chess is held on the day immediately before Art. Debate is held earlier in the week than Quiz. Drama is held neither on Monday nor on Saturday. Calligraphy is held exactly two days after Debate.

stem: Which one of the following could be the order of sessions from Monday to Saturday?
options: Debate, Quiz, Calligraphy, Drama, Chess, Art
Debate, Quiz, Chess, Art, Drama, Calligraphy
Debate, Quiz, Calligraphy, Chess, Art, Drama
Debate, Quiz, Calligraphy, Art, Drama, Chess
explanation: Test each option against the rules. Debate, Quiz, Calligraphy, Drama, Chess, Art satisfies every one. Each of the others breaks at least one rule: Chess is not on the day before Art; Drama is on Monday or Saturday; Calligraphy is not two days after Debate.

stem: Which one of the following cannot be true?
explanation: Calligraphy is held two days after Debate, so it cannot be earlier than Wednesday. Drama on Tuesday works in Debate, Drama, Calligraphy, Quiz, Chess, Art; Quiz on Saturday works in Debate, Drama, Calligraphy, Chess, Art, Quiz; Art on Tuesday works in Chess, Art, Drama, Debate, Quiz, Calligraphy.

stem: If Drama is held on Tuesday, which one of the following must be true?
explanation: Debate cannot be on Tuesday, which is Drama's day. Debate on Wednesday or Thursday would put Calligraphy on Friday or Saturday and leave no two consecutive free days for Chess and Art. So Debate is on Monday and Calligraphy on Wednesday. The other options fail in Debate, Drama, Calligraphy, Chess, Art, Quiz.

stem: Which one of the following could be true?
explanation: Drama on Thursday works in Debate, Quiz, Calligraphy, Drama, Chess, Art. Quiz cannot be on Monday because Debate comes first. Debate on Tuesday would put Calligraphy on Thursday, and the only consecutive free days for Chess and Art would be Friday and Saturday, which forces Drama onto Monday. Art on Wednesday would put Chess on Tuesday and force Drama onto Monday as well.

stem: On how many different days of the week could the Drama session be held?
explanation: Only five orders satisfy the rules: Debate, Quiz, Calligraphy, Drama, Chess, Art (Drama on Thursday); Debate, Drama, Calligraphy, Quiz, Chess, Art and Debate, Drama, Calligraphy, Chess, Art, Quiz (Tuesday); Chess, Art, Drama, Debate, Quiz, Calligraphy (Wednesday); Chess, Art, Debate, Drama, Calligraphy, Quiz (Thursday). So Drama can fall on Tuesday, Wednesday or Thursday, three days.

title: Red and Blue teams
text: Eight students from a school in Peshawar are divided into the Red team and the Blue team, with four students in each. The students are Uzma, Zainab, Faisal, Hina, Junaid, Maryam, Naveed and Sana. Uzma is in the Red team. Faisal and Hina are in the same team. Junaid and Maryam are in different teams. Sana is not in the same team as Faisal.

stem: Which one of the following could be the Red team?
explanation: Test each option against the rules. Uzma, Faisal, Hina, Junaid satisfies every one. Each of the others breaks at least one rule: Faisal and Hina are in different teams; Junaid and Maryam are in the same team; Sana is in Faisal's team.

stem: Which one of the following must be true?
options: Junaid is in the Red team
Zainab is in the Blue team
Sana and Hina are in different teams
Naveed is in the Blue team
explanation: Hina is always in Faisal's team, and Sana is never in Faisal's team, so Sana and Hina are never together. The other options fail in valid divisions: Naveed is Red in Uzma, Junaid, Naveed, Sana; Zainab is Red in Uzma, Zainab, Junaid, Sana; Junaid is Blue in Uzma, Zainab, Maryam, Sana.

stem: If Zainab is in the Red team, which one of the following must be true?
options: Junaid is in the Red team
Faisal is in the Blue team
Maryam is in the Blue team
Naveed is in the Red team
explanation: Red already holds Uzma, Zainab and one of Junaid and Maryam, who must be split, so only one place is left. Faisal and Hina need two places together, so they are both Blue. Sana cannot be with Faisal, so she joins Red. The Red team is then Uzma, Zainab, Sana and either Junaid or Maryam, so neither of those two is forced, while Naveed is always Blue.

stem: If Junaid is in the Blue team, which one of the following could be true?
options: Hina and Zainab are both in the Red team
Maryam is in the Blue team
Naveed is in the Red team
Zainab and Naveed are both in the Red team
explanation: Junaid in Blue puts Maryam in Red. Red: Uzma, Maryam, Naveed, Sana with Blue: Zainab, Faisal, Hina, Junaid satisfies every rule, so Naveed can be Red. Maryam cannot be Blue. Zainab and Naveed both in Red with Uzma and Maryam would leave Sana in Blue with Faisal and Hina. Hina and Zainab both in Red would bring Faisal too, so Red would be full without Maryam.

stem: If Sana and Zainab are in different teams, which one of the following must be true?
options: Naveed is in the Red team
Maryam is in the Red team
Junaid is in the Blue team
Faisal and Hina are in the Red team
explanation: Suppose Zainab were Red and Sana Blue. Faisal would then be Red, with Hina, making Red Uzma, Zainab, Faisal, Hina and putting Junaid and Maryam together in Blue, which is not allowed. So Zainab is Blue and Sana is Red. Faisal and Hina then go Blue, away from Sana, and Red needs two more: one of Junaid and Maryam, and Naveed.

title: Selection committee
text: A committee of four is to be chosen from seven nominees at a school in Quetta: Usman, Waqar, Yasir, Zara, Asad, Mehwish and Shahid. Usman and Zara are not both chosen. Waqar and Yasir are either both chosen or both left out. At least one of Asad and Mehwish is chosen. Shahid is chosen only if Waqar is chosen.

stem: Which one of the following could be the committee?
explanation: Test each option against the rules. Usman, Waqar, Yasir, Mehwish satisfies every one. Each of the others breaks at least one rule: Usman and Zara are both chosen; neither Asad nor Mehwish is chosen; Shahid is chosen without Waqar.

stem: Which one of the following must be true?
explanation: Suppose Waqar were left out. Yasir would be out as well, and Shahid could not be chosen, so the four members would have to come from Usman, Zara, Asad and Mehwish. That would include both Usman and Zara, which is not allowed. So Waqar, and with him Yasir, is always chosen. The other options each fail in some valid committee, for example Asad, Waqar, Yasir, Zara has no Usman, and Mehwish, Waqar, Yasir, Zara has no Asad.

stem: Which one of the following cannot be true?
options: Zara and Shahid are both chosen
Usman and Mehwish are both chosen
Shahid and Asad are both chosen
Zara and Mehwish are both chosen
explanation: Zara and Shahid together need Waqar and Yasir as well, which fills all four places and leaves neither Asad nor Mehwish. Each of the other pairs fits a valid committee: Mehwish, Usman, Waqar, Yasir; Asad, Shahid, Waqar, Yasir; Mehwish, Waqar, Yasir, Zara.

stem: If Usman is chosen, which one of the following must be true?
options: Asad and Mehwish are both chosen
explanation: Usman is chosen, so Zara is out. Waqar and Yasir are always chosen, which makes three members, and the fourth must be Asad or Mehwish, so Shahid is left out. Asad is not forced, since Mehwish can be chosen instead, and both together would make five.

stem: If Mehwish is not chosen, which one of the following could be true?
options: Shahid and Usman are both chosen
explanation: Without Mehwish, Asad is needed. With Waqar and Yasir also chosen, one place remains, and Zara can fill it (Asad, Waqar, Yasir, Zara). Asad cannot be left out, Waqar cannot be left out, and Shahid with Usman would make five members.

title: Dinner at a round table
text: Six guests, Saima, Talha, Usama, Wajiha, Yousaf and Zubair, sit at a round table in a restaurant in Islamabad. The six chairs are numbered 1 to 6 clockwise, so chair 6 is next to chair 1, and chairs 1 and 4, 2 and 5, and 3 and 6 are opposite each other. Saima sits directly opposite Talha. Usama sits next to Wajiha. Yousaf does not sit next to Talha. Zubair sits next to Talha.

stem: Which one of the following could be the seating, from chair 1 to chair 6?
options: Saima, Usama, Wajiha, Talha, Yousaf, Zubair
Saima, Usama, Zubair, Talha, Wajiha, Yousaf
Yousaf, Saima, Usama, Wajiha, Talha, Zubair
Saima, Talha, Zubair, Usama, Wajiha, Yousaf
explanation: Test each option against the rules. Yousaf, Saima, Usama, Wajiha, Talha, Zubair satisfies every one. Each of the others breaks at least one rule: Saima and Talha are not opposite each other; Usama and Wajiha are not neighbours; Yousaf sits next to Talha and Zubair is not next to Talha.

stem: Which one of the following must be true?
explanation: Put Saima in chair 1 and Talha opposite in chair 4; turning the table does not change the argument. Zubair must be next to Talha, in chair 3 or 5. Yousaf cannot be next to Talha either, so he cannot take the other of those chairs, and the only chairs left for him are 2 and 6, both next to Saima. The other options fail in Saima, Usama, Wajiha, Talha, Zubair, Yousaf: Usama is not next to Talha, Wajiha is not next to Saima, and Usama is not opposite Zubair.

stem: Which one of the following cannot be true?
explanation: Zubair sits next to Talha, and Talha is opposite Saima, so Zubair is two places away from Saima, never beside her. Usama next to Saima, Wajiha next to Talha and Wajiha opposite Zubair all occur, for example in Saima, Usama, Wajiha, Talha, Zubair, Yousaf.

stem: If Usama sits in chair 4, which one of the following could be true?
explanation: Usama in chair 4 puts Wajiha in chair 3 or 5. Talha, Zubair, Yousaf and Saima must fill the four other chairs in a row, in that order or the reverse, so Wajiha in chair 5 works in Zubair, Yousaf, Saima, Usama, Wajiha, Talha. Wajiha cannot be in chair 2, which is not next to Usama. Talha in chair 1 would put Saima opposite in chair 4, where Usama sits, and Yousaf in chair 5 would need both Saima and Zubair in chairs 4 and 6.

stem: If Usama sits next to Talha, which one of the following must be true?
explanation: Talha's neighbours are now Zubair and Usama. Usama's other neighbour is Wajiha, and Saima, opposite Talha, completes the circle between Wajiha and Yousaf, so the order round the table is Wajiha, Usama, Talha, Zubair, Yousaf, Saima. Wajiha is therefore next to Saima. Usama is not next to Saima or Yousaf, and Wajiha is not next to Talha.

title: Board exam timetable
text: A board holds six papers over three days, Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday, with exactly two papers a day, one in a morning session and one in an evening session. The papers are Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Maths, English and Urdu. Maths is held on an earlier day than Physics. Chemistry and Biology are held on the same day. English is held in a morning session. Urdu is not held on Wednesday. Physics is held in an evening session.

stem: Which one of the following could be the timetable, with the morning paper named first each day?
options: Mon Maths, English; Tue Urdu, Physics; Wed Chemistry, Biology
Mon Urdu, Physics; Tue Chemistry, Biology; Wed English, Maths
Mon Maths, Urdu; Tue English, Physics; Wed Chemistry, Biology
Mon English, Maths; Tue Physics, Urdu; Wed Chemistry, Biology
explanation: Test each option against the rules. Mon Maths, Urdu; Tue English, Physics; Wed Chemistry, Biology satisfies every one. Each of the others breaks at least one rule: Maths is not on an earlier day than Physics; English is in an evening session; Physics is in a morning session.

stem: Which one of the following must be true?
options: Urdu is held in a morning session
Maths is not held on Wednesday
explanation: Physics must be on a later day than Maths, so Physics cannot be on Monday, and Maths must be on Monday or Tuesday. Hence Maths is never on Wednesday, the option that must hold. Chemistry on Wednesday, Urdu in the morning and Physics on Tuesday each occur in some valid timetables but not in all.

stem: If Chemistry is held on Tuesday, which one of the following must be true?
options: Maths is held in a morning session
Biology is held in a morning session
explanation: Chemistry and Biology fill Tuesday, so Urdu, which cannot be on Wednesday, is on Monday. Maths cannot be on Wednesday, because Physics would then have no later day, so Maths is also on Monday. English and Physics fill Wednesday, so Physics on Tuesday is impossible. Maths and Urdu share Monday in either order, so Maths in the morning is not forced, and Biology may be in either session.

stem: If Urdu is held in a morning session, which one of the following must be true?
options: Maths is held in an evening session
explanation: Urdu is in a morning session, so its partner on the same day is in the evening. Chemistry and Biology are partners of each other, and English must be a morning paper, so Urdu's partner is Maths or Physics. If it is Maths, Maths is in the evening. If it is Physics, that day is Tuesday, Maths is on Monday and shares that day with English, who is in the morning, so Maths is again in the evening. The other options differ between valid timetables.

stem: If English is held on Tuesday, how many different timetables are possible?
explanation: English is in the Tuesday morning, so its evening partner is Maths, Physics, Urdu, Chemistry or Biology. Chemistry or Biology would split that pair. Maths would force Physics onto Wednesday with a partner who cannot exist, since Urdu is barred from Wednesday and Chemistry and Biology must be together. Urdu would leave Maths on Monday with Chemistry or Biology, again splitting the pair. So Tuesday is English and Physics, Maths and Urdu share Monday in either order, and Chemistry and Biology share Wednesday in either order, giving 2 × 2 = 4 timetables.

title: Sales postings
text: A company sends five representatives, Ahsan, Beenish, Chand, Dania and Ehtisham, to three cities: Lahore, Multan and Sialkot. Each representative goes to exactly one city, and every city receives at least one of them. Ahsan and Beenish are not posted to the same city. Chand is not posted to Lahore. Dania is posted either to Lahore or to the same city as Ehtisham. At most two representatives are posted to Multan. Beenish and Chand are posted to the same city unless Ehtisham is posted to Sialkot.

stem: Which one of the following could be the postings?
options: Lahore: Ahsan, Ehtisham; Multan: Beenish, Chand; Sialkot: Dania
Lahore: Ahsan, Chand, Dania; Multan: Beenish; Sialkot: Ehtisham
Lahore: Ahsan, Dania, Ehtisham; Multan: Beenish; Sialkot: Chand
Lahore: Beenish, Dania; Multan: Ahsan; Sialkot: Chand, Ehtisham
explanation: Test each option against the rules. Lahore: Beenish, Dania; Multan: Ahsan; Sialkot: Chand, Ehtisham satisfies every one. Each of the others breaks at least one rule: Chand is posted to Lahore; Dania is in Multan or Sialkot but not with Ehtisham; Beenish and Chand are in different cities while Ehtisham is not in Sialkot.

stem: If Ehtisham is posted to Lahore, which one of the following must be true?
options: Beenish and Chand are posted to the same city
explanation: Ehtisham is not in Sialkot, so the last rule applies and Beenish and Chand must be in the same city. Dania then has to be in Lahore, as she is with Ehtisham there. The other options are not forced: Ahsan may be in Multan or Sialkot, and Chand may be in either of those cities as well.

stem: If Ahsan is posted to Sialkot, which one of the following could be true?
options: Chand and Dania are posted to the same city
Beenish and Ehtisham are posted to the same city
explanation: Ahsan and Ehtisham in Sialkot, Beenish and Chand in Multan and Dania in Lahore is valid, so Beenish can be in Multan. With Ahsan in Sialkot, Ehtisham in Multan would not be in Sialkot, so Beenish and Chand would have to share a city. They cannot be in Lahore or Sialkot, so they would be in Multan, making three there. The same pressure stops Dania, Chand and Ehtisham, or Beenish and Ehtisham, from sharing a city.

stem: If Dania is posted to Multan, which one of the following must be true?
explanation: Dania is not in Lahore, so she must be with Ehtisham in Multan, which is then full. Ehtisham is not in Sialkot, so Beenish and Chand share a city. They cannot be in Multan, and Chand cannot be in Lahore, so both are in Sialkot. Lahore needs someone, and only Ahsan is left, so Ahsan is in Lahore.

stem: Which one of the following cannot be true?
options: Three representatives are posted to Lahore
Ahsan and Chand are posted to the same city
Three representatives are posted to Sialkot
explanation: If three were in Lahore, Multan and Sialkot would hold one each, and Chand would be alone in one of them. Beenish could not share his city, so the last rule needs Ehtisham in Sialkot, which puts Chand in Multan. Lahore then holds Ahsan, Beenish and Dania, which puts Ahsan and Beenish together. The other three options occur: Ahsan in Lahore, Beenish in Multan and the other three in Sialkot; Beenish in Lahore with Ahsan and Chand in Multan, Dania in Lahore, Ehtisham in Sialkot.

title: Club office-bearers
text: A club in Rawalpindi appoints three office-bearers from five members: Gulnaz, Hassan, Irfan, Javeria and Kamran. One member becomes Chairperson, a different member becomes Secretary and a third member becomes Treasurer. Gulnaz is not Chairperson. Hassan holds a post only if it is Treasurer. Irfan and Javeria do not both hold posts. Kamran is not Treasurer.

stem: Which one of the following could be the three office-bearers?
options: Chairperson Gulnaz, Secretary Irfan, Treasurer Hassan
Chairperson Irfan, Secretary Gulnaz, Treasurer Javeria
Chairperson Irfan, Secretary Gulnaz, Treasurer Hassan
Chairperson Hassan, Secretary Gulnaz, Treasurer Irfan
explanation: Test each option against the rules. Chairperson Irfan, Secretary Gulnaz, Treasurer Hassan satisfies every one. Each of the others breaks at least one rule: Gulnaz is Chairperson; Hassan holds a post other than Treasurer; Irfan and Javeria both hold posts.

stem: Which one of the following cannot be true?
options: Irfan is Chairperson and Javeria is Secretary
Kamran is Chairperson and Javeria is Secretary
Irfan is Chairperson and Gulnaz is Secretary
Javeria is Chairperson and Hassan is Treasurer
explanation: Irfan and Javeria are not both given posts, so they cannot hold two of the three posts together. Irfan as Chairperson with Gulnaz as Secretary, Kamran as Chairperson with Javeria as Secretary, and Javeria as Chairperson with Hassan as Treasurer are all possible: Irfan, Gulnaz, Hassan; Kamran, Javeria, Gulnaz; Javeria, Gulnaz, Hassan.

stem: If Kamran holds no post, which one of the following must be true?
explanation: Without Kamran, the posts go to three of Gulnaz, Hassan, Irfan and Javeria. Irfan and Javeria cannot both serve, so Gulnaz and Hassan both serve, with Irfan or Javeria. Hassan must be Treasurer, and Gulnaz cannot be Chairperson, so Gulnaz is Secretary. Irfan or Javeria is Chairperson, so neither of those is forced, and Hassan cannot be Secretary.

stem: If Hassan holds a post, which one of the following could be true?
explanation: Hassan, if he holds a post, is Treasurer, so Chairperson and Secretary come from Gulnaz, Irfan, Javeria and Kamran. Irfan as Secretary works with Kamran as Chairperson: Kamran, Irfan, Hassan. Gulnaz cannot be Chairperson, Kamran cannot be Treasurer and Hassan cannot be Secretary.

stem: If both Gulnaz and Kamran hold posts, in how many different ways can the three posts be filled?
explanation: Gulnaz and Kamran hold two posts, and the third goes to Hassan, Irfan or Javeria. With Hassan, he must be Treasurer, so Kamran is Chairperson and Gulnaz Secretary: 1 way. With Irfan or Javeria (call the person X), Gulnaz cannot be Chairperson and Kamran cannot be Treasurer. Of the 6 ways to place the three people, 2 have Gulnaz as Chairperson and 2 have Kamran as Treasurer, and 1 has both, leaving 6 − 2 − 2 + 1 = 3 ways for each of X. That gives 1 + 2 × 3 = 7 ways.

title: Two rows in the classroom
text: Six students sit in two rows of three seats in a classroom in Faisalabad. Seats 1, 2 and 3 are in the front row from left to right, and seats 4, 5 and 6 are in the back row, with seat 4 directly behind seat 1, seat 5 directly behind seat 2 and seat 6 directly behind seat 3. The students are Adeel, Bushra, Danyal, Eman, Fahad and Ghazala. Danyal sits directly in front of Bushra. Eman and Fahad sit in neighbouring seats of the same row. Ghazala does not sit in the middle column. Adeel does not sit in the same column as Bushra.

stem: Which one of the following could be the seating plan, listed from seat 1 to seat 6?
options: front row Adeel, Danyal, Eman; back row Fahad, Bushra, Ghazala
front row Danyal, Adeel, Ghazala; back row Bushra, Eman, Fahad
front row Adeel, Ghazala, Danyal; back row Eman, Fahad, Bushra
front row Adeel, Bushra, Danyal; back row Eman, Fahad, Ghazala
explanation: Test each option against the rules. front row Danyal, Adeel, Ghazala; back row Bushra, Eman, Fahad satisfies every one. Each of the others breaks at least one rule: Danyal is not directly in front of Bushra; Eman and Fahad are not in neighbouring seats of one row; Ghazala is in the middle column.

stem: Which one of the following must be true?
options: Adeel sits in the front row
Ghazala sits in the front row
Eman sits in the front row
Adeel sits in the middle column
explanation: If Danyal and Bushra shared the middle column, Eman and Fahad would have no two neighbouring free seats in either row, so Danyal and Bushra are in an end column. Each row then has two free seats, the middle one and the other end. Eman and Fahad fill both free seats of one row. Ghazala cannot take a middle seat, so she takes the end seat of the other row and Adeel its middle seat. Adeel is in the middle column. The other options fail in some valid plans: in Danyal, Eman, Fahad over Bushra, Adeel, Ghazala, Adeel and Ghazala sit at the back, and in Danyal, Adeel, Ghazala over Bushra, Eman, Fahad, Eman sits at the back.

stem: If Eman sits in the front row, which one of the following must be true?

Eman sits in the middle column

So the Bank is on floor 1. If the Clinic and the Lawyer were on floors 2 and 4, the Pharmacy and Tailor would take floors 3 and 5, putting the Tailor on floor 5, which is not allowed. title: Six cousins by height
text: Six cousins, Rehan, Shazia, Taimur, Uzma, Vaqar and Wajid, are compared by height, and no two have the same height. Rehan is taller than Shazia. Vaqar is shorter than Shazia. title: Training day timetable
text: A training centre in Faisalabad runs five sessions one after another, with no breaks, from 9:00 to 15:00. title: Four friends, subjects and cities
text: Four friends, Hasan, Ifra, Javed and Kausar, each study a different subject from Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics and Computer Science, and each lives in a different city from Lahore, Karachi, Peshawar and Quetta.
